'''Albert Pavlovich Baskakov''' ({{langx|ru|Альберт Павлович Баскаков}}; 1 March 1928 -  21 January 2012) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] and Russian scientist in the field of [[heat treating]] and a [[professor]] of thermophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://urfu.ru/?id=1010|title=Баскаков|website=urfu.ru|language=ru|access-date=2018-05-24}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Albert Pavlovich Baskakov was born in 1930 in [[Tver Oblast]], Russia.

In 1950, Baskakov graduated from the Faculty of Energo Mashinostroitelnythe of the [[Moscow Power Engineering Institute]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://thermalscience.vinca.rs/pdfs/papers-2015/in-memoriam-baskakov.pdf|title=In Memoriam Baskakov|access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref> After his graduation he remained at the institute to work and continue his studies, receiving the title of [[Candidate of Sciences|candidate of science]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://apbaskakov.ru|title=Главная - Сайт о выдающемся ученом Баскакове Альберте Павловиче|website=apbaskakov.ru|language=ru-RU|access-date=24 May 2018}}</ref>

== Career ==
Baskakov moved to the [[Ural State Technical University|Ural Polytechnic Institute]], where he worked as an Assistant Professor (1956-1964), Head of the Department (1964-1998), [[Professor]] (1998-2011) and Professor Consultant (2011-2012). From 1961 to 1963, he was responsible for the research laboratory of the Ural Branch of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences]]. In 1964, Baskakov became the head of the department of industrial heat and [[power engineering]]. His primary field of scientific interest was [[thermophysics]]: namely, the combustion and the use of solid fuels.

While at [[Ural State Technical University]], Baskakov created a scientific school on the study of fluidized systems and heat treatment of metals in a fluidized bed. In the 1980s, he developed a process of heat treatment of parts that was adopted by many enterprises of the [[Ministry of Defense Industry (Soviet Union)|defense industry of the USSR]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://xn----8sbanercnjfnpns8bzb7hyb.xn--p1ai/index.php/Баскаков_Альберт_Павлович|title=Энциклопедия Урала. Баскаков, Альберт Павлович}}</ref>

Baskakov led the construction of the first 10 MW Russia boiler with a circulating fluidized bed installed on a coal mine in Tulgan.<ref name=":5"/>

== Recognition ==
Throughout  1980s and 1990s, he received awards, including: fellowship of the RSFSR (1988), the N. A. Markevich NTO Mashpom the USSR (1983), and the top prize for the [[European Union]]'s competition for energy savings at its Energy Centre (1995).

Baskakov authored 15 textbooks and monographs and published over 600 journal articles, conference presentations and patients.<ref name=":5"/>

== Death ==
Baskakov died on January 21, 2012.

== Publications ==

* "Heat-energy basis of high-speed acid-free heating and thermal treatment in the fluidized bed"
